arxiv-2104-09558.title: The complex multi-scale structure in simulated and observed emission maps of the proto-cluster cloud G0.253+0.016 (‘the Brick’) 2021 The complex multi-scale structure in simulated and observed emission maps of the proto-cluster cloud G0.253+0.016 (‘the Brick’) – C
arxiv-2104-09558.creator: Maya A. Petkova, J. M. Diederik Kruijssen, A. Louise Kluge, Simon C. O. Glover, Daniel L. Walker, Steven N. Longmore, Jonathan D. Henshaw, Stefan Reissl, James E. Dale
arxiv-2104-09558.description: Abstract The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ; the central ∼ 500 \sim 500 pc of the Milky Way) hosts molecular clouds in an extreme environment of strong shear, high gas pressure and density, and complex chemistry. G0.253+0.016, also known as ‘the Brick’, is the densest, most compact and quiescent of these clouds.

arxiv-2106-08568.title: Towards Automated Attack Simulations of BPMN-based Processes
arxiv-2106-08568.creator: Simon Hacks, Robert Lagerström, Daniel Ritter
arxiv-2106-08568.description: Abstract Process digitization and integration is an increasing need for enterprises, while cyber-attacks denote a growing threat. Using the Business Process Management Notation (BPMN) is common to handle the digital and integration focus within and across organizations. In other parts of the same companies, threat modeling and attack graphs are used for analyzing the security posture and resilience.

arxiv-2110-08590.title: Automated Remote Sensing Forest Inventory Using Satellite Imagery
arxiv-2110-08590.creator: Abduragim Shtanchaev, Artur Bille, Olga Sutyrina, Sara Elelimy
arxiv-2110-08590.description: Abstract For many countries like Russia, Canada, or the USA, a robust and detailed tree species inventory is essential to manage their forests sustainably. Since one can not apply unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery-based approaches to large scale forest inventory applications, the utilization of machine learning algorithms on satellite imagery is a rising topic of research.

arxiv-2212-06148.title: Breaking Rate-Distance Limitation of Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Secret Sharing
arxiv-2212-06148.creator: Chen-Long Li, Yao Fu, Wen-Bo Liu, Yuan-Mei Xie, Bing-Hong Li, Min-Gang Zhou, Hua-Lei Yin, Zeng-Bing Chen
arxiv-2212-06148.description: Abstract Currently most progresses on quantum secret sharing suffer from rate-distance bound, and thus the key rates are limited. In addition to the limited key rate, the technical difficulty and the corresponding cost together prevent large-scale deployment. Furthermore, the performance of most existing protocols is analyzed in the asymptotic regime without considering participant attacks.

arxiv-2303-11745.title: Poisoning Attacks in Federated Edge Learning for Digital Twin 6G-enabled IoTs: An Anticipatory Study
arxiv-2303-11745.creator: Mohamed Amine Ferrag, Burak Kantarci, Lucas C. Cordeiro, Merouane Debbah, Kim-Kwang Raymond Choo
arxiv-2303-11745.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mohamed Amine Ferrag, Burak Kantarci, Lucas C. Cordeiro, Merouane Debbah, Kim-Kwang Raymond Choo. Federated edge learning can be essential in supporting privacy-preserving, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled activities in digital twin 6G-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) environments.

arxiv-2304-06975.title: HuaTuo (华驼): Tuning LLaMA Model with Chinese Medical Knowledge
arxiv-2304-06975.creator: Haochun Wang, Chi Liu, Nuwa Xi, Zewen Qiang, Sendong Zhao, Bing Qin, Ting LiuResearch Center for Social Computing and Information Retrieval,Harbin Institute of Technology, China{hcwang,cliu,nwxi,zwqiang,sdzhao,bqin,tliu}@ir.hit.edu.cn
arxiv-2304-06975.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs), such as the LLaMA model, have demonstrated their effectiveness in various general-domain natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Nevertheless, LLMs have not yet performed optimally in biomedical domain tasks due to the need for medical expertise in the responses.

arxiv-2308-03486.title: Improving Mass Detection in Mammography Images: A Study of Weakly Supervised Learning and Class Activation Map Methods
arxiv-2308-03486.creator: Vicente Sampaio \inst 1, Filipe R. Cordeiro \inst 1, Vicente Sampaio, Filipe R. Cordeiro
arxiv-2308-03486.description: Abstract In recent years, weakly supervised models have aided in mass detection using mammography images, decreasing the need for pixel-level annotations. However, most existing models in the literature rely on Class Activation Maps (CAM) as the activation method, overlooking the potential benefits of exploring other activation techniques.

arxiv-2404-04523.title: On the vorticity threshold for steady water waves
arxiv-2404-04523.creator: Evgeniy Lokharu, Miles H. Wheeler
arxiv-2404-04523.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Evgeniy Lokharu, Miles H. Wheeler. One of the most striking features of two-dimensional steady water waves with adverse vorticity is the emergence of stagnation points in the flow, even along branches of solutions that are initially unidirectional. In this paper we show that, for constant adverse vorticity above a certain explicit threshold, the first stagnation point must appear on the bed directly below the crest.

arxiv-2602-11183.title: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Continuous Navigation via Memory-Augmented Kalman Filtering
arxiv-2602-11183.creator: Yin Tang, Jiawei Ma, Jinrui Zhang, Alex Jinpeng Wang, Deyu Zhang
arxiv-2602-11183.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yin Tang, Jiawei Ma, Jinrui Zhang, Alex Jinpeng Wang, Deyu Zhang. Continuous navigation in complex environments is critical for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). However, the existing Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) models follow the dead-reckoning, which iteratively updates its position for the next waypoint prediction, and subsequently construct the complete trajectory.

arxiv-2606-19910.title: Light-weight Pronunciation Assessment via Discrete Speech Token Surprisal
arxiv-2606-19910.creator: Syeda Faiza Ahmed, Shammur Absar

pmc-10733568.title: Extracellular vesicle‐associated cholesterol supports the regenerative functions of macrophages in the brain
pmc-10733568.creator: Sam Vanherle, Jeroen Guns, Melanie Loix, Fleur Mingneau, Tess Dierckx, Flore Wouters, Koen Kuipers, Tim Vangansewinkel, Esther Wolfs, Paula Pincela Lins, Annelies Bronckaers, Ivo Lambrichts, Jonas Dehairs, Johannes V Swinnen, Sanne G S Verberk, Mansour Haidar, Jerome J A Hendriks, Jeroen F J Bogie
pmc-10733568.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Macrophages play major roles in the pathophysiology of various neurological disorders, being involved in seemingly opposing processes such as lesion progression and resolution. Yet, the molecular mechanisms that drive their harmful and benign effector functions remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that extracellular vesicles (EVs) secreted by repair‐associated macrophages (RAMs) enhance remyelination ex vivo and in vivo by promoting the differentiation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs).

pmc-11457438.title: Interactions between Struvite and Humic Acid and Consequences on Fertilizer Efficiency in a Nonacidic Soil
pmc-11457438.creator: Javier Erro, Iñigo Seminario, José M. García-Mina
pmc-11457438.description: The effect of humic acid extracted from peat (AHt) on improving the struvite (STR) fertilizing efficiency is explored. To this end, a soil incubation study is correlated to plant assays comparing STR, STR-AHt, and superphosphate (SSP). Characterization techniques confirm the incorporation of the AHt into the STR.

pmc-11516575.title: Climate change and its health effects - an optional subject for medical students
pmc-11516575.creator: Z Abram
pmc-11516575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The Standing Committee of European Doctors urged to include training on the impact of climate change on health for health professionals. Currently, in the curriculum of most medical schools, the health-related impacts of climate change represent a peripheral part. The teaching of health effects of climate change should be made part of the training of health professionals and should be introduced in the curriculum of medical schools.

pmc-11715741.title: Proteomics‐Based Prediction of Hippocampal Atrophy in the General Population
pmc-11715741.creator: Meilin Chen, Zhibo Wang, Yuye Ning, Jianping Jia
pmc-11715741.description: BackgroundHippocampal atrophy is being characterized as a key biomarker in neurodegenerative disease, especially for dementia. Nevertheless, detecting hippocampus relied on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), it's very costly and time‐consuming. Our objective is to develop a predictive score to detect MRI‐related hippocampal volume based on large‐scale blood proteomics.

pmc-12391016.title: Lung Transplantation Following Paraquat Poisoning: Time to Think
pmc-12391016.creator: Hari Kishan Gonuguntla, Somesh Tripathi, Vimi Varghese, Sricharan Goda, Chetan Rao Vaddepally, Balasubramoniam Kavumkal Rajagopalan, M. Sheetal Kumar, Belgundi Preeti Vidyasagar
pmc-12391016.description: Paraquat, a commonly available herbicide, when consumed in high doses, affects organs with high blood flow (lungs, heart, kidney and liver), leading to pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory failure and death. Few reports of rescue lung transplantation exist. Complete depletion of paraquat from the body is necessary prior to transplant; however, timing for and concerns after lung transplantation remain unknown.

pmc-12399481.title: Correction to: Safety and Effectiveness of Glargine 300 U/ml After Switching from Basal Insulins in Patients with Type 1 Diabetes: COMET-T Study
pmc-12399481.creator: Stefan Gölz, Julia K. Mader, Stefan Bilz, Julia Kenzler, Thomas Danne
pmc-12399481.description: e “From baseline (54.3%), TIR changed at week 12 (mean change 0.3% [± 14.3]; p = 0.8383) and at week 24 (+ 4.5% [± 14.9], p = 0.078)” should have read “From baseline (54.3%), TIR changed at week 12 (mean change 0.3% [± 14.3]; p = 0.8383) and at week 24 (+ 3.0% [± 14.9], p = 0.078).

pmc-12558097.title: Mandibular Advancement Devices for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Bibliometric Analysis (1984–2024)
pmc-12558097.creator: Suliman Alsaeed, Ikram Ul Haq
pmc-12558097.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo conduct a bibliometric analysis of scientific publications on mandibular advancement devices (MADs) for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), evaluating publication trends, citation impact, productive countries, institutions, authorship patterns, and keyword co-occurrence to identify key contributors and research directions.Materials and MethodsA comprehensive search was performed in the Web of Science Core Collection on May 12, 2025, using topic-specific keywords related to MADs and oral appliances. The search covered literature published from 1984 to December 31, 2024.

pmc-12640369.title: Efficacy of Plant-Based Iron and Vitamin C in Adults With Iron Deficiency Anemia: A Randomized, Double-Blind Clinical Study
pmc-12640369.creator: Maheshvari N Patel, Nayan Patel, Jit Maheshvari
pmc-12640369.description: BackgroundIron-deficiency anemia (IDA) is a common nutritional disorder marked by low hemoglobin and impaired oxygen transport, leading to fatigue and reduced quality of life. This study assessed the efficacy and safety of two plant-based iron formulations in adults with IDA.

pmc-12784739.title: Assessing Natural Weaning in Suckler Beef Cattle: A Single-Farm Retrospective Data Analysis of Calf-Raising Success and Colostrum Antibody Uptake in the Absence or Presence of a Yearling Calf
pmc-12784739.creator: Dorit Albertsen, Peter Plate, Suzanne D. E. Held
pmc-12784739.description: Simple SummaryCommercial suckler beef calves are commonly physically separated from their dams at four to ten months old, often causing stress and health issues in cows and calves. This retrospective study looked at a ‘natural weaning‘ approach where cows kept their calves and therefore had a yearling still with them when the next calf was born.

pmc-12976211.title: Hepatic embolization for Cushing syndrome from metastatic tumors: a single-center case series
pmc-12976211.creator: Shuyao Zhang, Jorge Esteban Mosquera, Clive Musonza, Anil K Pillai, Jessica Abramowitz, Sasan Mirfakhraee, Patricio M Polanco, Salwan Al Mutar, Waddah Arafat, Oksana Hamidi
pmc-12976211.description: BackgroundCushing syndrome (CS) from metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) or neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) presents a therapeutic challenge when surgery is not feasible. Liver-directed embolization, including bland transarterial embolization (TAE) and yttrium-90 (Y-90) radioembolization, may palliate hypercortisolism arising from hormonally active hepatic metastases.

pmc-13107467.title: Nonenergy Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage (BiCRS): Assessing Durability of Nongaseous Carbon Products Across Terrestrial Storage Fates
pmc-13107467.creator: Sinéad M. Crotty, Peter W. Reiners, Leah K. Clayton, Edward Young, Andrew Jones, Melissa A. Cregger, Anne K. Starace, Anne E. Harman-Ware
pmc-13107467.description: Biomass Carbon Removal and Storage, or BiCRS, pathways use plants or algae that remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis and store it underground or in long-lived products. While some BiCRS approaches generate an energy product, all BiCRS approaches generate a carbon product.

pmc-13125009.title: Structural Characterization of Squid Peptides and Evaluation of Their Antiphotoaging Activity in Nude Mice
pmc-13125009.creator: Yuan Peng, Minghui Tian, Xiaoyu Liu, Fangcheng Su
pmc-13125009.description: Solar exposure is a major cause of skin photoaging, and this damage is known to be alleviated by natural antioxidants. In this study, four novel squid cyclic peptides (SCPs) with potential antiphotoaging activity were isolated via activity-guided fractionation based on their antiphotoaging effects.

pmc-13437944.title: Seroprevalence of Brucellosis in Cattle, Sheep, and Goats in the Southeastern Region of Bangladesh
pmc-13437944.creator: F M Yasir Hasib, Md Sirazul Islam, Chandan Nath, Md Moktadir Billah Reza, Md Masuduzzaman, Sharmin Chowdhury, Lipi Buch
pmc-13437944.description: Brucellosis is one of the major bacterial zoonoses worldwide. Bangladesh is an endemically affected country with this neglected disease. This cross‐sectional study aimed to estimate the seroprevalence of brucellosis among cattle, goats, and sheep in the southeastern part of Bangladesh, covering Chattogram and Khagrachhari districts.
